newsitem.title: UK: London gold seen firming after New York opens.
newsitem.headline: London gold seen firming after New York opens.

text.p: Gold prices are expected to push into the mid-$350s per ounce after New York opens on Tuesday, dealers said.
Before that, however, gold would have to hold above its opening levels around $352.50, which was established after a firm close in New York on Monday and subsequent steadiness in the Far East.
Gold fixed at $352.60, up from Monday's $350.25 and its close of $350.50/$351.00.
"Everybody was bearish yesterday, now they're bullish today. It's that kind of market," one dealer said.
Sentiment began to change on Monday after Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he had heard of no plans for other central banks to sell gold from their reserves.
His remark came after a regular G10 meeting and referred to last week's news that Switzerland intends to sell gold to establish a humanitarian fund for victims of the Holocaust and other tragedies.
"There was some good quality producer selling yesterday but the U.S. funds stepped in. We have seen the Swiss buying today," a dealer said.

The dealer noted Swiss banks had been very active in the gold options market late last week following the announcement of Switzerland setting up a humanitarian fund and revaluing its gold reserves, which would take two years to legislate.
There was buying of $325 puts and granting of calls, but in a quieter options market this week volatilities had drifted lower, dealers said.

"It seemed to be co-ordinated," one dealer said, adding that the business could have been done to prevent banks being on the wrong side of the market when surplus material and the gold to establish the fund was sold in a couple of years time.
Around 800 tonnes of gold would be sold over 10 years.
Dealers saw gold staying in the mid-$350s today. "There really isn't much reason for speculators to come into the market right now," said one dealer.
Silver held its firmer opening levels without attracting much attention. It was at $5.25/$5.27, up seven cents.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer on Japanese buying.
Dealers cited the continued impasse over Russian exports and the threatened strike at the Norilsk mining and refining plant.
Platinum was $4.60 firmer at $382.50/$383.50 and palladium up $3.40 at $154.50/$155.50.
